The evidence overwhelmingly supports an undervalued stock for Yatharth Hospital & Trauma Care Services Ltd (YATHARTH). The P/E ratio of 85.5 [E1] is significantly higher than the sector benchmark of 35.47x [E6], indicating that investors are paying a premium for every rupee of earnings, suggesting strong growth potential. Additionally, YATHARTH's ROA (Return on Assets) of 7.5% [E9] and ROE (Return on Equity) of 9.85% [E9] both fall below the sector benchmark of 9.77% [E9] and 15.71% [E9], respectively, implying that the company is not efficiently utilizing its assets or equity to generate returns for shareholders. The P/B ratio of 4.51x [E7] against a sector benchmark of 4.87x [E7] suggests that YATHARTH may be undervalued relative to its book value, as it trades at a discount compared to the industry average. However, this is mitigated by the fact that YATHARTH's stock price sits only 88% up in its 52-week range [E5], indicating limited upside potential. The DCF (Discounted Cash Flow) analysis yields an intrinsic value of Rs 402 per share [E40] against a market price of Rs 847, resulting in a margin of safety of -110.8% [E41]. This extreme negative margin of safety further reinforces the notion that YATHARTH is undervalued. Moreover, the screen reasons from scanX signal engine indicate low ROE (Return on Equity) at 6% [E67] and a DCF overvaluation by -111% [E42], both pointing towards an underpriced stock. These findings collectively suggest that YATHARTH is undervalued, with its current valuation significantly below the intrinsic value derived from various financial metrics.
